_readme: User-visible changes in the replacement app, newest first.

entries.summary: Vocabulary choice now says progress carries over and you can switch any time
detail: The line under 'Choose your flashcard vocabulary source' adds: What you learn carries over, and you can switch at any time.
Shown on the inline choose screen (desktop and mobile) and in the in-study vocabulary picker; both read the same wording.

entries.summary: Consistent username wording throughout the profile flow
detail: Profile labels, guidance, validation and playlist sign-in messages now say username.
Existing usernames, saved profiles and learning progress are preserved.

entries.summary: Birthday is optional when choosing a learning profile
detail: Leave day and month blank to look up profiles by name alone.
A supplied birthday narrows matching names; profiles without a birthday remain discoverable.
Partially entered or invalid birthdays still receive inline feedback.

entries.summary: A clearer, quieter welcome and profile screen
detail: Welcome offers a clear saved-progress path and a lighter guest option.
The profile form has one heading, shorter guidance and no repeated welcome pitch.

entries.summary: Quick tutorial first, with the full card tour in Help
detail: The tutorial introduction now starts with the essential lesson, including the correct pronunciation controls.
The full card tour remains an explicit option in Help and the introduction.
All five first-time UX audit recommendations are implemented and recorded.

entries.summary: Clarify learning language prompt, add known-languages primer, and expand tutorial notes
detail: Prompt explicitly asks for 'Choose the language you’re learning' to avoid confusion for non-native English speakers.
Add post-language selection primer asking which languages the learner already knows to filter look-alikes via Smart Skip.
Expand tutorial with Smart Skip explanation and reassure learners that they can switch between Speech and Lyrics anytime with progress saved.

entries.summary: Names and birthdays identify separate learning profiles
detail: Enter a username/name and birthday day/month, with inline validation and no birth year.
Matching profiles show language and last study date; an exact match can always create a separate profile.
Existing initials and all progress keep their original IDs; selected profiles remain remembered on this device.
Saved sets are isolated by profile; the progress backend now includes a shared profile directory.

entries.summary: A shorter first lesson and one-time swipe guidance
detail: Automatic onboarding covers reveal, pronunciation, grading and moving on; Help retains the full card tour.
The first real card reveal shows swipe guidance outside the card until a successful grading swipe.

entries.summary: Reliable keyboard sign-in and phrases-panel resume
detail: Study shortcuts pause while signing in, so Enter submits Continue normally.
Stopping on a phrases panel saves the parent word; older panel snapshots recover by word.

entries.summary: Spanish cognate mapping for Portuguese learners
detail: Spanish is now available as a known language for Portuguese cognate filtering.
Maps each shown meaning through the Spanish dictionary and CogNet; 4,257 of 10,000 current Portuguese cards qualify at the initial 0.80 cutoff.
English mappings are preserved; false friends and cards with unmatched meanings remain in study.

entries.summary: Clearer main-page level and account controls
detail: Level example words exclude phrases and multi-word expressions, with slightly brighter text.
Selected level is larger with less vertical padding.
Language and learner initials are larger; tutorial and settings icons are white.

entries.summary: Tutorial fits its actual available space, including Bigger text
detail: Measured card height from the rendered tutorial area after navigation appears, replacing fixed window-height allowances.
Reserved header and button space, including app text zoom, and held card dimensions steady between steps.
Kept scrolling inside card content and independently inside desktop explanations when needed.

entries.summary: SpanishDict senses sharing a context are one row again; topic chips show only when they tell rows apart
detail: kilo: "kilo" and "kilogram" are one SpanishDict meaning (context "kilogram") and now share one row instead of two rows with separate meters; irse "to go" / "to leave" (to exit a place) likewise. Context grouping had been switched off for every provider on 2026-09-29 because Wiktionary contexts are labels ("intransitive"); it is back for SpanishDict only.
The 10% main-card floor measures a SpanishDict context as a whole, as the card shows it, so a meaning split 2 + 2 between kilo and kilogram is not dropped.

Topic chips (mostly Portuguese Wiktionary) appear only when they tell a row from another row with the same translation, and only the most specific one: massa "dough" lost "cooking | food | lifestyle", garganta's two "throat" rows lost "anatomy | medicine | sciences". The topics stay in each row's (i) note.
Display only: no WSD, release or menu change.

entries.summary: Tutorial layout grows with the browser while card size stays steady
detail: Desktop cards use the available window height and width, with room reserved for navigation.
The tutorial header stays fully visible, and explanations spread across wider screens.
Opening meanings keeps the card size constant; mobile retains its separate height budget and internal scrolling.

entries.summary: Taller desktop tutorial cards and no practice-skip button
detail: Removed Skip this practice; the top-right close button remains available.
Wide desktop cards are about 17% taller while preserving space for Back and Next.
Narrow desktop layouts put the explanation and navigation beside the card, allowing a taller card without pushing buttons off-screen.
Phone cards reserve space for the longest explanation and remain the same height throughout the tutorial.

entries.summary: Each subsense row now needs 10% of a card's sentences to stay on the main card
detail: The 10% floor used to pool rows sharing an English translation, so a one-sentence slip rode on its siblings: estuve "I was (to fit)" rested on a misread "estuve pensando" while the five "I was" rows held 35% together.

Now each subsense row is measured on its own and anything under 10% moves to Rarer uses with its sentences. estuve drops "to fit" and "to be located"; darte drops "to give (to generate / to motivate)"; pt tem keeps "to own" and "general use".
If a translation's rows clear 10% together but each is under it, its largest row stays.
Function words (prepositions, articles, pronouns, conjunctions) keep pooling by translation, since their grouping is curated.
Both providers (SpanishDict and Wiktionary).

entries.summary: Keep the tutorial example and source visible; scroll overflow instead of clipping
detail: Example boxes no longer shrink or impose a height cap, so their source icons and footer remain intact.
Compact cards fit the space above the coach and navigation, without their bottom falling outside the visible card area.
Meaning rows scroll when expanded content exceeds available space; very short screens also allow scrolling through the card contents.
Retains the complete 13-step Portuguese tutorial.

entries.summary: Keep the tutorial card height fixed while meanings expand
detail: Tutorial cards retain their height across flips, opening or closing meaning groups, selecting a meaning, and cycling examples.
Overflowing meanings scroll inside the card; long examples scroll within their own area.
Card height responds only to viewport size; Back and Next stay outside the card and visible.
Preserves meaning-list scroll position when selecting a meaning or another example.

entries.summary: Restore all card explanations to the main tutorial
detail: The full Portuguese tutorial again includes word rank, part of speech, dictionary form, frequency, meanings, useful extras, commonness, examples, and source explanations.
Meaning and example practice are part of the full sequence; no explanations require an optional details detour.
Retains the larger controls, improved contrast, full-size phone tap targets, and scrollable card layout.

entries.summary: End of a new-word set shows what happened, not an accuracy score
detail: Ring centre '20/25 known'; green known arc over an amber Practice track.
Boxes read '✓ Known' and '→ Added to Practice' (amber) instead of Correct / Missed.
Each card counts once, by its last answer (attempt totals double-counted re-shown cards).
Perfect Set and confetti when every card is known. Practice sessions keep the accuracy ring.

entries.summary: Progress screens show one percentage each
detail: Deck overview (on load / back to menu): the ring now fills to '% of speech understood' (lyrics: 'of these lyrics understood'); the separate '% cards known' figure is gone.
Its legend keeps the card counts (Known / Practice / New) as plain numbers, without colour keys.
Loading a set is unchanged: the ring counts cards known in that set.
End of set: the '72% accuracy' line under the title is gone; the ring already says it.

entries.summary: Source chooser: no chevrons, Best for under the description, fuller speech card, shorter intro
detail: Chevrons removed from Everyday speech and Your music (the whole card is the button); Spotify strip keeps its arrow.
'Best for' sits directly under the description in both cards at every width.
Speech: 'From films and TV shows — the everyday words people actually use when they talk to each other.' plus Best for 'Understanding films and TV shows'.
Intro: 'Your flashcards come from this source, most common words first.'

entries.summary: Source chooser: Spotify now sits inside the Your music card
detail: 'Connect your Spotify' is the footer of the Your music card (full width, green tint, arrow) instead of a loose pill under the page, on phone and desktop.
Desktop: 'Best for' follows the description in both cards so the two line up.
The note under 'Choose your flashcard vocabulary source' is one step brighter.
These changes shipped inside commit 24201107 (shared staging area with another session); this entry records them.

entries.summary: Short hands-on card tutorial, clearer controls, and full-size phone cards
detail: Five-step speech lesson: recall, flip, choose a meaning, cycle an example, then start studying; optional card details remain available.
Lyrics shares the lesson and adds song credits and playback, without a second tutorial.
Phone cards scroll above the coach without shrinking text or tap targets; all meanings remain accessible on small screens.
Clear finish and Next buttons, focused explanation text, honest grammar examples, and no resume prompt covering the tutorial.
Practice works by keyboard; returning from card details preserves the learner’s selected meaning and example.
Narrow desktop windows keep their active instruction and navigation visible beside the scrollable card area.

entries.summary: Small text raised to 11px everywhere; bigger Smart Skip switch target; heading order fixed
detail: 117 style rules below 11px (8-10.5px labels like WELCOME, BEST FOR, RECOMMENDED, stats labels) now 11px; plus the card's 'Possible meanings' label.
Smart Skip switch answers taps across its whole cell (about 74x50) without looking bigger.
'Send a note' and the Smart Skip admin heading are h3, not h4, so screen readers get the right order.
From an Impeccable audit: undersized-text flags at phone width 31 -> 0, skipped headings 2 -> 0.

entries.summary: Smart Skip fast-forward icon back on desktop
detail: The icon shows when the row is 600px or wider; phones keep the slim two-line row.

entries.summary: Smart Skip row fits on phones; desktop shows example skipped words
detail: Removed the fast-forward icon, the chevron and its red dot, and the divider before the switch.
Info icon is now red, like the ones beside Choose level and Choose a set.
Rows 600px or wider show real example words: 'Look-alikes like padre, tres, idea' when off, 'Skipping padre, tres, idea, …' when on.

entries.summary: Smart Skip row: line under the name says what it does, not Off
detail: Off: 'Fewer cards, same coverage'. On: 'N words skipped'. The switch alone shows on or off.

entries.summary: Set pills lose their outline and spread out; Smart Skip 'Details' becomes an info icon
detail: No yellow or green outline on set pills; only the chosen set has a ring. Gap 8 to 9px.
The 'Details' word on the Smart Skip row is now an information icon.

entries.summary: Smart Skip row reads as one control: state line, Details cue, solid red Recommended pill
detail: Under the name: 'Off', or 'On · N words skipped' (accent coloured when on).
'Details ›' on the right says the row opens the details page; the switch alone turns it on.
'Recommended' is a solid red pill with white text.
